transcript: tonight, my boyfriend Paul and I attended the first preview of Pictures from Home, a new Broadway play adapted from Larry sultan's photo memoir of the same name. in it, Larry is capturing his parents in their daily lives while revisiting and analyzing old home photos and videos. one of the main themes and a point of conflict, is whether or not photos illustrate people or merely imitate and perform versions of them. ultimately, I think the best way I can describe the show is like a stage version of a portrait, multifaceted and endlessly able to be analyzed. it was at times humorous, at times tense, and at times poignant, much like real life. overall, I enjoyed the show, although it took me a bit to settle into the dialogue, and at times I found it to be a little slow. but as this was the first preview, I'm really interested to hear what other people think, especially as the show evolves on its way to opening night. and with that, another playbill for my collection.
